S64.01.note: The site may first ask for access with a card 'AGI needs access to <host>' (Allow for this task, Always allow on this site, Decline).
steps: Open a normal website in a tab and open the side panel (toolbar AGI icon).
In the Chat tab, click the + button labelled Add attachment, then click Add the browser page.
Type a question that depends on the page, such as what the page says about a named topic, and send it.
Check the answer uses the content of the open page, and that the page chip shows the site's host.
S64.01.where: Chat tab > + (Add attachment) > Add the browser page

S64.02.needs: a normal website and the site approved in Extension settings
S64.02.note: If the site is not approved the notice reads 'Approve <host> in Extension settings to add text selected there.' Right-clicking a selection also offers 'Explain this' and 'Translate this' in apps/extension/src/background.ts.
steps: On a normal website, highlight a sentence or paragraph with the mouse.
Open the side panel and click the + button labelled Add attachment.
Click Add selected text, then type a question about the highlighted text and send it.
Check the answer refers to the highlighted text.
S64.02.where: Chat tab > + (Add attachment) > Add selected text

steps: Open a normal website and right-click an empty part of the page (not a link, image or text).
Click Summarize this page in the menu.
The side panel opens with the page attached; wait for the reply.
Check the reply summarizes the page that is open in the tab.
S64.05.where: Right-click page background > Summarize this page

labels.text: Ask one question about this page…

S64.06.needs: an approved website and the Page assistant overlay setting on
S64.06.note: The overlay mounts only on approved origins when the setting is on (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts). Its default state was not found in the code. The Options page setting is in the Options section (apps/extension/src/features/options/preference-rows.ts).
steps: Open a website that you have approved for AGI, and make sure the side panel is closed (the launcher hides while it is open).
Click the round Ask AGI launcher button on the page.
Type a question about the page into the box labelled Ask one question about this page… and press Enter.
Check the streamed answer uses the visible text of this page.
S64.06.where: Website tab > Ask AGI launcher (round button at the edge of the page) > text box 'Ask one question about this page…'

S64.07.note: Typed questions in the box send the visible page text, not the transcript (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts submitComposer); only the three video chips read captions. Videos without captions get a 'no captions' reply.
steps: Open a YouTube video that has captions, on an approved site.
Click the Ask AGI launcher on the page.
Click the chip Summarize video (or Key timestamps, or Q&A).
Wait for 'Reading the video captions…', then check the answer is about what is said in the video.
S64.07.where: YouTube watch page > Ask AGI launcher > Summarize video, Key timestamps or Q&A

S64.08.note: The shortcut is set in the manifest (apps/extension/manifest.json) and can be changed in Chrome's shortcut page.
steps: Open the side panel with the toolbar AGI icon, or the shortcut Command+Shift+K on Mac.
In the Chat tab, ask a question and wait for the answer.
Switch to a different website tab and come back to the side panel.
Check the same conversation is still shown, then click New chat and check a new empty conversation starts.
S64.08.where: Toolbar AGI icon (or Open AGI side panel shortcut) > Chat tab

S64.10.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
S64.10.note: No separate Open URL control was found; the navigate tool is used inside a Computer Use task. Only http and https addresses are allowed.
steps: Open a normal website tab and open the side panel, then click the Computer Use tab.
If the panel asks, click the Allow browser control button for the site.
Type in the Task box a goal such as 'Open https://example.com' and click Start.
Check the tab goes to that address and the Assistant steps list shows the opening step.

S64.14.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
S64.14.note: No separate search control was found; website search is done as a Computer Use task.
steps: Open a website that has its own search box and open the Computer Use tab.
In the Task box type a goal such as 'Search this site for a term and read me the first three results', then click Start.
Watch the Assistant steps list as the search is typed and submitted.
Check the reply reads back the results shown on the page.

S64.15.needs: a web form and a signed-in AGI account
steps: Open a job application form on an approved site (Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby for Run Autofill).
Open the Computer Use tab and click Run Autofill.
For another form, type in the Task box a goal such as 'Fill the name and email fields with the details I give you' and click Start.
Check the fields show the values that were asked for, and that password and payment fields were left alone.
S64.15.where: Computer Use tab > Run Autofill (job application pages), or Computer Use tab > Task > Start (other forms)

S64.16.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
steps: Open a website with several linked pages and open the Computer Use tab.
In the Task box type a goal with several steps, such as 'Find the contact phone number on this site, then open the pricing page and read the first price', and click Start.
Watch the Steps counter (Steps: n/max) and the Assistant steps list climb over several actions.
Check the run ends with an 'Agent finished' entry and the answer covers both parts of the goal.

S64.17.needs: a website that declares WebMCP tools
S64.17.note: The agent's tools discover_site_tools and call_site_tool are in apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/browserToolDefinitions.ts. Whether the agent picks a site tool is its choice, and the write-tool dialog is window.confirm in apps/extension/src/webmcp.ts.
steps: Open a website that publishes WebMCP tools (none is named in the code, so find one first).
In the Computer Use tab type a task the site's tool can do, and click Start.
Check Assistant steps shows a call to the site's tool rather than only clicks.
For a tool that changes data, check the page shows a confirmation dialog that must be accepted before the call runs.
S64.17.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a website that declares its own tools

S64.18.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
steps: Start any Computer Use task (see Task and Start).
While it runs, click the Assistant steps toggle to open the list.
Watch each action appear as it happens, with its time.
Check the list matches the actions the tab takes, and the last entry is the final report.

S64.19.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
S64.19.note: The code shows screenshot thumbnails added as the agent takes them, not a continuous live stream. The live view is the Chrome tab the task runs in.
steps: Start a Computer Use task and open Assistant steps.
Watch the browser tab itself, which is the task's visible page.
When an entry titled 'Screenshot captured' appears, click its thumbnail to view it larger.
Check the thumbnail shows the current state of the page.
S64.19.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps > Screenshot captured

S64.20.note: A tab already in a Chrome tab group is not regrouped (apps/extension/src/background.ts markComputerUseTab). The right-click item Add Tab to AGI Group is a separate manual control.
steps: Open a normal website tab that is not already in a Chrome tab group.
Start a Computer Use task on that tab (Computer Use tab > Task > Start).
Look at the Chrome tab strip for a blue group titled AGI around that tab.
After the run ends, check the tab has left the group.
S64.20.where: Chrome tab strip: during a Computer Use run the tab is put in a blue tab group titled AGI

S64.21.needs: a site that asks you to sign in during a task, a signed-in AGI account, an approved site
S64.21.note: The hand-off is requested by the agent's ask_user_to_take_over tool (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts). The Take over and Continue controls are the same ones used here.
steps: Start a Computer Use task on a site that needs you to sign in (for example a site with a login page).
Wait for the banner titled 'Your turn' to appear.
Click Take over, sign in on the page, then click Continue.
Check AGI carries on with the task after Continue and the run reaches Agent finished.
S64.21.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a site that asks you to sign in during the task

S64.22.needs: a page that shows a CAPTCHA or human check, a signed-in AGI account, an approved site
S64.22.note: The agent is told never to solve a CAPTCHA itself (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts).
steps: Start a Computer Use task on a page that shows a CAPTCHA or 'I am not a robot' check.
Wait for the banner titled 'Your turn' to appear.
Click Take over, solve the check on the page, then click Continue.
Check AGI resumes the task after Continue.
S64.22.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page that shows a CAPTCHA or human check

S64.25.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
steps: Start a Computer Use task that takes several actions.
While it runs, click Stop, or click Take over to pause AGI.
Check the Stop control changes to Stopping… and the run ends.
Check a banner titled 'Browser control stopped' appears and no more actions happen on the page.
S64.25.where: Computer Use tab > Stop (shown while a run is active), or Take over

S64.26.needs: a page that offers a file to download
S64.26.note: Downloads are always asked for (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts). The code shows the approval card and the step list; no separate downloads list was found.
steps: Start a Computer Use task that downloads a file from a page.
Before the download, check an approval card appears titled 'Approve action: download_file'.
Read the card, then click Allow or Skip.
Check the step 'Download: <address>' is listed in Assistant steps.
S64.26.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page that offers a file to download

steps: Have a small file ready on the computer.
Start a Computer Use task that needs to upload that file to a page.
When the card 'Approve file upload' appears, click Choose files to upload and pick the file. Check the preview lists it and nothing has been sent yet.
Click Allow to send it, or Skip, and check the result shown in Assistant steps.
S64.27.where: Computer Use tab > Task > Start, on a page with a file upload control

S64.28.needs: a normal website tab to test with
S64.28.note: The site-access card in chat offers Allow for this task, Always allow on this site and Decline (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json).
steps: Click More in the side panel, then Extension settings.
Click Permissions and find the Browser access section and the Browser control choice (Auto, Ask first, Full access, YOLO).
Open a normal website, then reopen Options and use Add or Remove for the current site in the approved sites list.
Under Blocked sites click Block for a site, then check that site is removed from approved sites and AGI no longer reads it.

S64.32.needs: a signed-in AGI account and an approved site
S64.32.note: The chat summary text is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts.
steps: Run a short Computer Use task and wait for it to finish.
Open Assistant steps and look at the last entry titled 'Agent finished'.
Check its text lists what was done and the result.
Open the Chat tab and check it shows 'The browser task finished.' followed by the report.
S64.32.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps > Agent finished
